# Methods (auto-generated by nf-codonyat 0.3.1)

**Research use only.** These outputs are descriptive (QC, contamination report,
read-mapping based subtype estimate, consensus sequence, codon and amino-acid
frequencies). They contain no drug-resistance or clinical interpretation.

FASTQ samples were quality-checked with FastQC 0.12.1 and trimmed with fastp 1.3.6.
A contamination report was produced with Kraken2 2.1.6 against the database
`kraken2_tiny_db` (report only; no reads were removed; a warning is raised when HIV-1 is
below 50% of classified fragments or human reads exceed 50% of all fragments).
An HIV-1 subtype estimate was obtained by competitive read mapping with BBSplit (BBMap 39.18)
against the panel `hiv1_subtype_panel_v1` (bins A, B and group M consensus), reported as the % of reads
assigned unambiguously to each bin (read-mapping based; research use only).
Overlapping read pairs were merged with BBMerge (BBMap 39.18); merged reads (single-end)
and unmerged pairs (paired-end) were aligned with Bowtie2 2.5.4 (`--very-sensitive-local`) to the
annotated reference and combined with samtools 1.21 / 1.24. Alignments with MAPQ < 20
or flags 0x904 were removed. Strand metrics were additionally computed from an alignment
of the unmerged (pre-merge) read pairs. A consensus sequence was called with iVar 1.4.4
(threshold 0.5, IUPAC codes for mixtures, minimum depth 100x with N below it, minimum base
quality 20; insertions at >= 0.5; majority deletions applied). Codon frequencies per protein
(all) were computed with codonyat 1.1.0 and summarised as amino-acid frequency tables.
Reports were collated with MultiQC 1.35.

## Notes

- Single-end FASTQ samples skip read merging and the strand-metrics alignment. SAM inputs enter at the alignment filter; the FASTQ-only steps (FastQC, fastp, Kraken2, subtype estimate, merging, Bowtie2) do not apply to them.

- bowtie2 2.5.4
- codonyat 1.1.0
- fastp 1.3.6
- fastqc 0.12.1
- ivar 1.4.4
- kraken2 2.1.6
- multiqc 1.35
- pigz 2.8
- python 3.12.14
- samtools 1.21 / 1.24
